title: Does CoT Length Predict Unfaithfulness Under Hint Injection?

original_idea.body: Does CoT Length Predict Unfaithfulness Under Hint Injection? Problem: whether longer reasoning is more or less likely to silently use a planted hint is open. Direction: inject hints into MCQ items on a small reasoning model, bin trajectories by CoT length, test whether acknowledgment and flip rates correlate with CoT length; use the cot-unfaithfulness harness as scaffold.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: testing CoT-length-as-monitoring-heuristic directly informs monitor design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited cot-unfaithfulness harness + binning by length.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused correlation analysis; reuses existing scaffold.

low_compute.reasoning: Small reasoning model on MCQ, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Hint-unfaithfulness studied; the length-correlation angle is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Hint-injection is established; correlating unfaithfulness with CoT length is plausibly open.
